mostWorthwhile.text: Following fallen wood through fungal decomposition, soil nutrients and renewed growth made the nutrient cycle tangible and explained how fungi feed.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial inspections of forest, cells, soil and wetland all returned no partners, making the search for a starting point repetitive.

surprise.text: Waterlogged ground slows decomposition enough for peat to accumulate and potentially store carbon underground for millions of years.

arbitrary.text: Using partnered cells with fallen wood to produce fungi was not obvious until the compatibility report; the result clarified that it represents evolution, not wood turning into fungi.

continue.text: Yes. The connected nutrient, carbon and water cycles made me curious about what another chapter might explain, despite the frustrating opening search.
